title: Your local shrine
hook: a shrine may be closer than you think

segments.voice: Yesterday, Lourdes and Fatima as pilgrims, where wheelchairs lead the procession and volunteers push. Your line was the sick go first.

Forty minutes up the highway, past a gas station and a feed store, a small brown sign marks a turnoff. A gravel road. A grotto made of fieldstone, with a statue of Mary and rows of candles in red glass. A rack of rosaries left by people who prayed and went home. On a weekday afternoon, a retired couple sits on a bench, a man in work boots kneels on the gravel, and a woman reads the handwritten notes tucked into the stones. None of them flew anywhere. Some drove past it for years before stopping.
screen: `A SMALL BROWN SIGN OFF THE HIGHWAY.` → `A GROTTO OF FIELDSTONE.` → `NOBODY FLEW ANYWHERE.`

segments.voice: First, what a shrine is. The Church's Code of Canon Law defines one simply: a church or other sacred place that the faithful visit on pilgrimage for a particular reason of devotion, with the local bishop's approval. So a shrine is measured not by size or fame but by prayer: people come on purpose. Then, the oldest pattern. In Genesis, Jacob is running from his brother. He stops for the night at an ordinary spot, puts a stone under his head, and dreams of a ladder reaching to heaven. He wakes and says, in effect, the Lord was in this place and I didn't know it. He calls it the house of God, then sets the stone up as a pillar, pours oil on it, and names the place Bethel. He didn't travel to a famous holy site. He found one on the road he was already on. Why do local shrines matter? A grand pilgrimage may come once in a lifetime, and some people can never make one: too sick, too poor, too busy caring for someone. A shrine a drive or a bus ride away is a pilgrimage for the rest of us. It can hold a grandparent's devotion, a parish's history, an immigrant community's patron saint, brought from home. Your diocese's website or parish office can tell you which shrines are near. Some sit beside a big church; some are a single statue at the edge of a cemetery. The pilgrimage can be an afternoon, and the prayer the same.
screen: `A PLACE PEOPLE VISIT TO PRAY.` · `JACOB'S STONE PILLOW AT BETHEL.` · `A PILGRIMAGE FOR THE REST OF US.` · `ASK THE PARISH OR THE DIOCESE.` · then, large: `THE LORD WAS IN THIS PLACE.`

segments.voice: Think of places within an hour of you where people go to pray: a grotto, a statue at a crossroads, a chapel you've driven past, a side altar with candles always lit. Picture pulling off the road and walking in with a name, a worry or a thank-you. If you pray, offer that intention now and promise to bring it in person; if you don't, just choose the place.
Your local shrine. A church or sacred place near you that people visit on pilgrimage, with the bishop's approval. A pilgrimage in an afternoon. Today's word.
Your line: close to home. A shrine doesn't need to be famous, only prayed in. Rest well.

howItsDone: Catholics visit diocesan and national shrines near home for a day of prayer, Mass and confession; dioceses and parishes list approved shrines and sometimes organize local pilgrimages to them.

chat.says: Does a shrine have to be famous, like Lourdes, to count as one?
options: No; Church law calls it a place people visit to pray, with the bishop's approval.
Yes; only the pope can name a shrine, and only after a miracle happens there.
No; any place with a statue of Mary counts, and no bishop is involved.
chat.meaning: Canon law defines a shrine as a sacred place the faithful visit on pilgrimage for devotion, with the local bishop's approval; size and fame don't matter.

grotto.meaning: a small cave, or a cave-like shrine, often holding a statue

diocese.meaning: a church region led by a bishop

notes: Index hook 'most dioceses have a shrine within reach' is a count claim; the teaser hook and script avoid it.

Canon 1230 paraphrased: a church or other sacred place to which the faithful make pilgrimage for a special reason of piety, with the approval of the local ordinary. Confirm, and confirm the Latin term 'sanctuarium'.

Genesis 28 paraphrased (Jacob's words are given 'in effect', not quoted). 'Bethel, house of God': Genesis 28:19 names the place Bethel; the meaning 'house of God' is from Jacob's words in 28:17. Confirm.
Most-claims avoided; 'a grand pilgrimage may come once in a lifetime' is hedged; confirm.
The hook's grotto is an invented composite scene, not a named shrine.
